subject: Acme - Pricing & cost model follow-up
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acme.com>
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - Pricing & cost model follow-up

Hi Maria —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery:

Summary of what you shared:
- Primary use: customer support summarization + contextual assistants across product pages.
- Monthly active users (MAU): ~120k (North America).
- Expected average requests per MAU/day: ~0.8 (mix of short prompts + 1 longer summarization prompt).
- Average tokens per request: 450 tokens (prompt+response) average; 1,200 tokens for heavy summarization flows.
- Target monthly token range (your ask): 30M–75M tokens/month.
- Budget guidance you mentioned: $30k–$50k/month target initially; room to scale with committed discount.

Initial unit economics we discussed (ballpark):
- Baseline hosted unit price (no commit): $1,200 / 1M tokens (model-weighted estimate across mix).
- Committed/Reserved capacity estimate (monthly commit): $550–$700 / 1M tokens depending on model and commitment term.
- Target you mentioned during the call: ~$600 / 1M tokens as an ideal target to land within budget.

Action items / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the conservative and aggressive monthly token estimates (e.g., conservative = 30M, aggressive = 75M)? I attached a quick volume worksheet for you to drop numbers into (acme_monthly_volume.xlsx).
2) Ill run a detailed invoice estimate and send a line-item cost model (by EOD tomorrow) showing: per-model unit price, expected tokens, and optional reserved capacity discounts.
3) If numbers look reasonable, we can scope a 7–14 day pilot with a capped spend and telemetry to validate unit economics in prod traffic.

Attached: acme_monthly_volume.xlsx (volume worksheet) — Ill follow up with the pricing calculator and PDF invoice estimate.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Acme - Pricing & cost model follow-up

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the recap — that’s helpful. A few clarifications and updated numbers from our side:

- Conservative monthly tokens: ~28M (we'll be conservative for Q3 ramp).
- Expected steady-state (6 months+): ~62M/month.
- Peak daily concurrency: ~1.2k concurrent inference requests (mostly short chat flows).
- Model preference: we’re prioritizing quality for the summarization path (higher token usage) but are open to cost-optimized variants for chat.
- Budget: initial PO we can commit to is $35k/month, with room to increase to $50k if the pilot demonstrates ROI.

Can you include line items for both (a) hosted pay-as-you-go and (b) 12-month reserved capacity (committed) with sample unit pricing for both the high-quality model and a cost-optimized model? Also, a quick note on how caching/prefix reuse might reduce billable tokens for the chat flows would be great.

Thanks — Maria
Maria Gonzalez
Head of Product Ops, Acme Corp
maria.gonzalez@acme.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acme.com>
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - Pricing & cost model follow-up

Maria —

Appreciate the updated numbers. I ran the model and attached: acme_pricing_calculator.xlsx (editable) and acme_invoice_estimate.pdf (PDF summary). Key highlights below (rounded):

Assumptions used:
- Conservative tokens: 28,000,000 / month
- Steady-state tokens: 62,000,000 / month
- Mix: 70% chat (avg 350 tokens/request) + 30% heavy summarization (avg 1,200 tokens/request)

Line-item estimate (monthly) — hosted PAYG:
- Model: high-quality (rw-large-v1): effective blended price: $1,150 / 1M tokens
  - 28M tokens => $32,200
  - 62M tokens => $71,300

Line-item estimate (monthly) — 12-month reserved commit (examples):
- Committed tier A (12mo): $600 / 1M tokens (requires ~50% commit of expected steady-state)
  - If you commit to 35M/month => effective monthly cost: $21,000 (plus overage at PAYG rate)
- Committed tier B (12mo): $520 / 1M tokens (larger commit / longer term)
  - If you commit to 60M/month => effective monthly cost: $31,200

Estimated one-time onboarding & infra setup (optional): $6,000 (invoiced once).

Notes on optimizations:
- Prefix / KV caching for chat flows: could reduce billable tokens by ~8–18% depending on reuse. We modeled a conservative 10% reduction for chat traffic in the calculator.
- Batching and quantized model variants reduce per-token execution cost (reflected in the committed tiers).

Target unit economics (your stated target ~ $600 / 1M tokens) is achievable with a modest commit + pilot that validates caching opportunities.

Next steps I propose:
1) You review the attached sheets and confirm the commit band you’re comfortable with.
2) We prepare a short SOW (Marissa will draft) for a 14-day pilot with a $7k capped spend, monitoring, and success metrics.
3) If pilot meets SLAs and unit economics, we convert to a 12-month reserved commitment.

I’ve attached the files and included a one-page PDF estimate for your procurement team. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want to walk through the calculator live.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: acme_pricing_calculator.xlsx, acme_invoice_estimate.pdf
